reproduction_method: fresh independent requests against the live target; exact reproducible requests below; controls and null cases included per each finding

findings.title: Unauthenticated GET /rest/memories exposes all user accounts (password hashes, deluxe tokens, email, role) with no authorization check
findings.analysis: Observation (2026-10-05T03:48:39Z): GET http://lab-mutator:3000/rest/memories with no Authorization header returns HTTP 200 (application/json; charset=utf-8, 6134 bytes) and returns all 10 memory records; each record embeds a full user object as a stringified dict containing fields never exposed by the public UI: email (bjoern@owasp.org), 32-hex password hash (9283f1b2e9669749081963be0462e466), role (deluxe), 32-hex deluxeToken (efe2f1599e2d93440d5243a1ffaf5a413b70cf3ac97156bd6fab9b5ddfcbe0e4), and totpSecret. Example record UserId=13, id=1. Reasoning: a bogus Authorization: Bearer header changes nothing (response identical), so the endpoint performs no authorization at all. Impact: Sensitive Data Exposure (maps to the app's own Password Hash Leak challenge family, id=1). Caveat: the embedded user object is delivered as a stringified dict rather than a nested JSON object; the exposed deluxeToken value is not a valid signed JWT (presenting it as Authorization: Bearer returns 401 'no header in signature'), so its session-hijack value is reduced, but the exposure of password hashes plus session tokens remains. Scope: route-specific (other user-bearing routes gated), not a global misconfiguration.
findings.false_positive_check: 1) Control comparison: /rest/wallet/balance, /rest/basket, /rest/user/authentication-details and /api/SecurityAnswers/ all return HTTP 401 without an Authorization header, proving the application's authorization mechanism works elsewhere; the leak is route-specific. 2) The embedded user data contains non-public fields (password, deluxeToken) that no legitimate public memory listing would return. 3) Response is stable across independent fresh requests (6134 bytes, same user records) and the bogus Bearer header leaves the response byte-identical. 4) A full user record was captured repeatedly with the same email, password hash, deluxeToken and role. 5) Query parameters orderBy/limit/skip/where are ignored by this endpoint (still returns full catalog of 10 records), so pagination params do not restrict the exposure.

findings.title: Unauthenticated POST /api/SecurityAnswers/ persists records (missing authentication on write endpoint)
findings.analysis: Observation (2026-10-05T03:48:39Z): GET http://lab-mutator:3000/api/SecurityAnswers/ (no Authorization header) -> HTTP 401, so the read path is authorized. POST /api/SecurityAnswers/ with Content-Type application/json, body {"questionId":7,"answer":"verify-new","email":"verify@repro.test"} and NO Authorization header -> HTTP 201 with a persisted record (id=26). A repeat POST of the identical payload -> HTTP 201 with a NEW record (id=28), proving server-side persistence without ownership or deduplication checks. An empty-object POST -> HTTP 201 with id=27 (no input validation). Reasoning: the mutation selectively removed server-side authorization from writes on this endpoint while the read path and neighboring writes remain gated. Impact: Broken Access Control / Missing Authentication on write. An unauthenticated actor can create arbitrary security-answer records in this store. Note: answers are hashed server-side (64-hex); the unauthorized write itself is the verified property. Neighboring POST endpoints (Complaints, Cards, Addresses, Reviews, Questions, Memberships) correctly return 401 or 500.
findings.false_positive_check: 1) The identical route requires auth for GET (401), so this is not a public diagnostic endpoint; the gap is write-specific (read-gated, write-open). 2) A repeat POST of the identical payload created a new row (id 26 -> 28), proving server-side persistence without ownership checks. 3) Empty-object POST -> 201 with id=27, proving no input validation gates the write. 4) POST with an Origin: http://evil.example header still -> 201 id=29: CORS does not gate the write; the behavior is endpoint-specific rather than global (neighbors gated). 5) IDs are monotonically incremental (seed ~25, then 26, 27, 28, 29 on this boot), confirming server-side insertion rather than client-controlled ids.

findings.title: SQL injection in GET /rest/products/search?q= bypasses the product filter, disclosing the complete product catalog
findings.analysis: Observation (2026-10-05T03:48:39Z): GET http://lab-mutator:3000/rest/products/search?q=Apple -> HTTP 200, 921 bytes, 3 products (ids 1, 24, 47). GET http://lab-mutator:3000/rest/products/search?q=%27%20OR%20%271%27=%271 -> HTTP 200, 16557 bytes, 46 products (the complete catalog). The injected tautology string ' OR '1'='1 occurs in zero product catalog names (0 of 46), yet the response returns the entire product set, so benign string filtering cannot explain it. Malformed payloads (e.g., ?q=' UNION SELECT 1,2,3--) -> HTTP 500 with raw SQLite errors ('near "UNION": syntax error'), proving raw input reaches a SQLite query layer. A LIKE-comment probe (q=test'%2D%2D) also returns 500. The deduced query structure is a LIKE filter concatenating the raw q value (WHERE name LIKE '%' || <q> || '%'). Pagination/order parameters (orderBy/limit/skip/where) are ignored (full catalog always returned), consistent with q being the sole filter. Impact: Injection (filter bypass). An unauthenticated actor can disclose the full product dataset beyond any intended search scope. Explicit limitation: a boolean TRUE/FALSE data-extraction channel could not be reproducibly established; the AND-branch contradiction always evaluates zero-rows and the OR-branch tautology always evaluates all-rows, so no column-level extraction (users/passwords) via this parameter is claimed. The malformed-payload raw SQLite errors demonstrate SQL-layer execution but do not by themselves yield data.
findings.false_positive_check: 1) Malformed payloads elicit raw 'SQLITE_ERROR' messages, proving raw input reaches a SQLite query layer rather than a client-side filter. 2) The injected tautology payload occurs in 0 of 46 product names, yet returns the full catalog of 46; a benign filter cannot produce this. 3) Behavior is stable across independent fresh requests (921 vs 16557 bytes, identical id sets) and matches the prior activation's independent reproduction byte-for-byte. 4) The finding is scoped strictly to filter bypass and full-catalog disclosure; data extraction via this parameter is explicitly unclaimed because the extraction channel was not reproducible. 5) Pagination/order params orderBy/limit/skip/where return the full catalog regardless, consistent with the q value being the sole (and unsafely concatenated) filter.

findings.title: Unauthenticated GET /metrics exposes mutation-introduced operational telemetry (Prometheus endpoint not present in pinned v20.2.0 baseline)
findings.analysis: Observation (2026-10-05T03:48:39Z): GET http://lab-mutator:3000/metrics with no Authorization header returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type 'text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8' (~26113 bytes; live gauge counters increment by ~50 B between scrapes). Output includes Prometheus-format counters (juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_output_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_tool_calls_total, http_requests_count by status_code, juiceshop_startup_duration_seconds). The pinned v20.2.0 base image serves no /metrics endpoint, so this is a mutation-introduced observability surface. Reasoning: the endpoint is accessible with zero authorization, exposing internal operational telemetry (request counts by status, startup timing, and LLM usage counters) to any unauthenticated actor. Impact: Observability Failure (maps to the app's own Exposed Metrics challenge family, id=97). Scanning all metric lines for secret/password/token/key/credential/api_key/bearer/x-api patterns found no emitted secrets or credentials; the exposure is limited to operational telemetry. Behavior is stable across independent fresh requests (200, text/plain, same gauges; only request counters increment between scrapes).
findings.false_positive_check: 1) The pinned v20.2.0 base image (bkimminich/juice-shop@sha256:8739101ade29358abb5469ee66ae78e582c97ed0a5543a4ad102e5fa5193526b) serves no /metrics endpoint, so this is a mutation-introduced route rather than baseline behavior. 2) Authorization: the endpoint returns 200 with no Authorization header while auth-gated routes (e.g., /rest/basket, /rest/user/authentication-details) correctly return 401, proving the app's auth mechanism works elsewhere and exposure is route-specific. 3) Output was scanned for secret/password/token/key/credential/api_key/bearer/x-api patterns; only HELP text lines match the generic word 'token', with no emitted secrets. 4) Response is stable across independent fresh requests, ruling out a transient leak.
